title: Chapter 6: Bengal Renaissance & Social Reform Movement

blocks.content: The Bengal Renaissance (19th century) was one of the most important socio-cultural reform  movements in Indian history. It transformed Bengal and India with modern ideas.
The Bengal Renaissance was not merely a cultural revival, but an intellectual awakening that redefined social consciousness and laid the bedrock for modern India.

rows: Monotheism, anti-idol worship, rights for women, abolition of Sati.
Radical rationalism, freedom of thought and expression, questioning traditions.
Synthesis of Vedantic spirituality with practical social service and humanitarian work.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Raja Ram Mohan Roy established the Brahmo Sabha in 1828 to oppose idol worship, polytheism, and social evils like Sati.
Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar campaigned extensively for female education and played a vital role in legalizing widow remarriage through the Hindu Widows' Remarriage Act XV of 1856.
Henry Vivian Derozio led the Young Bengal Movement, inspiring radical free thought and rational critique of traditional socio-religious dogmas.
The movement created an intellectual awakening that blended Western rationalism with traditional Indian philosophy, paving the way for Indian nationalism.
Regulation XVII of 1829 declared the practice of Sati illegal and punishable by criminal courts under Governor-General Lord William Bentinck.
Bethune School, established in Calcutta in 1849 with Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar as secretary, was a major landmark for women's education.
The Young Bengal Movement was heavily influenced by the French Revolution and rationalist philosophy.
